scenes.text: A *16-year-old* did *$150K* in sales with ChatGPT and a Walmart run
scenes.say: Real story. A sixteen-year-old did one hundred and fifty thousand dollars in sales, with ChatGPT and a Walmart run.

scenes.title: Who: *Ethan Alexander*, 16
lines: Kansas City, Missouri. He quit lacrosse and suddenly had time on his hands.
Started May 2025 with $500 left to him by his great-grandfather.
First product: Walmart laundry detergent, resold on Amazon.
scenes.say: Meet Ethan Alexander, sixteen, from Kansas City, Missouri. He quit lacrosse and suddenly had time on his hands. In May twenty twenty-five he started with five hundred dollars left to him by his great-grandfather. His first product? Walmart laundry detergent, resold on Amazon.

scenes.title: The *AI* part
lines: He trained ChatGPT to write Python code that filtered out products that wouldn't sell.
Used AI to track inventory and stay organized.
A seller app showed him fees, stock and the price he needed to profit.
scenes.say: Here's the AI part. He trained ChatGPT to write Python code that filtered out products that wouldn't sell. He used AI to track his inventory and stay organized, and a seller app showed him the fees, the stock, and the price he needed to make a profit.

scenes.title: The *grind*
lines: Drove 30 to 40 minutes to every big Walmart in the metro, buying out the shelf.
Summer nights packing orders until 5 or 6 a.m.
Then Target, Menards, Home Depot, and pallets stacked in his parents' garage.
scenes.say: Then came the grind. He drove thirty to forty minutes to every big Walmart in the metro, buying out the shelf. Summer nights were spent packing orders until five or six in the morning. Then he added Target, Menards, Home Depot, and pallets stacked in his parents' garage.

scenes.title: The *numbers*
lines: Biggest day: about $6,000 in sales, roughly $2,000 profit.
Hired virtual assistants to keep up, all while in high school full time.
scenes.say: Now the numbers. Ten thousand dollars in sales in month one. His biggest day: about six thousand dollars in sales, roughly two thousand in profit. He hired virtual assistants to keep up, all while in high school full time.

scenes.label: in sales in *10 months*
scenes.sub: SALES, NOT PROFIT. SOURCE: ENTREPRENEUR, JULY 2026
scenes.say: In ten months: one hundred and fifty thousand dollars in sales. That's sales, not profit, as reported by Entrepreneur in July twenty twenty-six.

scenes.title: What *now*
lines: He paused the hustle after $150K to focus on school and new projects.
Part of the money goes toward college: business or psychology.
"I just took what was in front of me and made it mine." Entrepreneur, Amanda Breen, July 15, 2026.
scenes.say: So what now? He paused the hustle after hitting one-fifty K to focus on school and new projects. Part of the money goes toward college, business or psychology. In his words: I just took what was in front of me, and made it mine.
